blocks.text:
After breakfast, a city tour of Buenos Aires with an English-speaking guide, lasting about 3 hours.

La Boca welcomes you with colorful facades and the streets of the old port district. San Telmo is known for its old houses, bars and antique shops. Plaza de Mayo is home to the Casa Rosada, the presidential palace associated with the country's political history and Eva Perón.

Along the way, you will see the Obelisk, Avenida 9 de Julio, Recoleta and modern Puerto Madero. Just a few blocks separate the old port from grand architecture and office towers, so the city keeps changing as the tour unfolds.

La Boca and San Telmo retain their links to the city's port history, while Recoleta feels much quieter and more formal. Puerto Madero, in contrast, shows modern Buenos Aires with new buildings and waterfront promenades. This route brings together very different neighborhoods in just a few hours, making the city tour a useful starting point for a free day.
